quests.instruction: What do we call the spot where two sides of a shape meet?
quests.hint: Touch the place on a square where one side turns into the next side.
quests.explanation: A corner is the point where two sides meet. A triangle has three of them, and a square or rectangle has four.
quests.funFact: Picture frames are built by joining four sides together at their corners.

quests.instruction: A paper banner has these shapes in a row: circle, triangle, circle, square, circle. How many circles are on the banner?
quests.hint: Point to each circle one at a time and count only those.
quests.explanation: The circles are in the first, third, and fifth spots, so there are three of them.
quests.funFact: Bunting and banners are often made from repeating shapes because they are easy to cut from paper.

quests.instruction: Which of these is not shaped like a rectangle?
quests.hint: Check each object for straight edges and four corners.
quests.explanation: A garage door and a bar of chocolate have straight sides and four square corners. A hula hoop is a ring that curves all the way around.
quests.funFact: The hula hoop craze took off in 1958.

quests.instruction: Sam dips the bottom of a soup can in paint and presses it on paper. What shape is the print?
quests.hint: Trace the flat bottom of a can with your finger and notice what happens at the edge.
quests.explanation: The bottom of a can is flat and round, with a smooth edge and no corners, so its print is a circle.
quests.funFact: The top and bottom of a can are two matching circles.

quests.instruction: Two squares of the same size are pushed together so they share one full side. What shape do they make?
quests.hint: Compare how long the new shape is with how tall it is.
quests.explanation: The new shape is twice as long as it is tall and still has four square corners, so it is a rectangle and no longer a square.
quests.funFact: Putting equal squares side by side in a single row always makes a rectangle.

quests.instruction: Lena sorts shapes into two piles: has corners and no corners. Which shape goes in the has corners pile?
quests.hint: Run a finger around each shape and see which one makes you turn.
quests.explanation: A triangle has three corners where its straight sides meet. A circle and an oval are smooth all the way around, so they belong in the other pile.
quests.funFact: Sorting things by a rule is how libraries and grocery stores keep things organized.

quests.instruction: A floor is covered with square tiles that fit together with no gaps. Which of these shapes could also cover a floor with no gaps?
quests.hint: Think about which shape has straight sides that can sit flat against each other.
quests.explanation: Copies of a triangle can sit edge to edge with no empty spaces. Circles and ovals curve away from each other and leave gaps.
quests.funFact: Many bathroom floors are tiled with squares, rectangles, or six-sided hexagons.

quests.instruction: Marco counts four corners on a flat shape that has only straight sides. How many sides does it have?
quests.hint: Walk along the edge. Each time you reach a corner, a new side begins.
quests.explanation: On a shape with straight sides, each corner is where one side ends and the next begins, so there are as many sides as corners.
quests.funFact: A triangle has three sides and three corners, and a square has four of each.

quests.instruction: Zoe draws three straight lines to make a triangle. What must be true for it to really be a triangle?
quests.correctAnswer: The lines must join with no gaps
options: The lines must all be the same length
The lines must join with no gaps
The lines must all point upward
quests.hint: Think about whether the shape is shut in all the way around.
quests.explanation: A triangle is a closed shape, so its three sides have to touch at their ends. Triangles can have sides of different lengths and can point in any direction.
quests.funFact: A shape with a gap in it is called an open shape.

quests.instruction: An egg seen from the side is closest to which shape?
quests.hint: Is it exactly as wide as it is tall, or stretched one way?
quests.explanation: An egg has a smooth curved edge with no corners, and it is longer one way than the other. That makes it an oval, not a circle.
quests.funFact: Not all eggs are oval. Owl eggs are nearly round.

quests.instruction: Which shape can be cut into two triangles with one straight cut?
quests.hint: Look for a shape with corners that a straight cut could join.
quests.explanation: A straight cut from one corner of a rectangle to the opposite corner leaves two triangles. A circle and an oval have no corners, so a straight cut cannot make triangles.
quests.funFact: Triangles are the simplest straight-sided shapes, so bigger straight-sided shapes can be built from them.

quests.instruction: A tall rectangle is squeezed until all four of its sides are the same length. What shape is it now?
quests.hint: Compare the sides of the shape after it has been squeezed.
quests.explanation: A shape with four corners and four equal sides is a square. Squeezing the long sides until they match the short ones turns the rectangle into a square.
quests.funFact: A square is a rectangle whose sides are all equal.

quests.instruction: A snowman picture uses three circles stacked up, two small circles for eyes, and a triangle for the nose. How many circles are in the picture?
quests.hint: Count the big circles and the small ones, but not the nose.
quests.explanation: Three big circles plus two small eye circles make five. The nose is a triangle, so it is not counted.
quests.funFact: In Japan, snowmen are traditionally built with two balls of snow instead of three.

quests.instruction: Look at a triangle, a square, and a rectangle. Which one has a different number of corners from the other two?
quests.hint: Count the corners on each shape and see which count does not match.
quests.explanation: A square and a rectangle each have four corners, but a triangle has only three, so it is the odd one out.
quests.funFact: Squares and rectangles are close relatives because both have four square corners.

quests.instruction: Which group has more corners in total: two triangles or one square?
quests.hint: Count the corners in each group, then compare the totals.
quests.explanation: Two triangles have 3 + 3 = 6 corners, while one square has only 4.
quests.funFact: Adding the same number twice, like 3 + 3, is the start of multiplication.

quests.instruction: A toy car needs wheels that roll smoothly. Which shape should the wheels be?
quests.hint: Think about a shape with no corners to bump along the ground.
quests.explanation: A circle is the same distance across everywhere and has no corners, so it rolls without bumping. Square or triangle wheels would thump over each corner.
quests.funFact: The center of a rolling circle stays at the same height the whole time.

quests.instruction: Which two shapes have the same number of corners?
quests.hint: Count the corners on both shapes in each pair, then check whether the counts match.
quests.explanation: A square and a rectangle both have four corners. A triangle has three, and a circle has none, so the other pairs do not match.
quests.funFact: A square and a rectangle both have four corners, but only the square has four equal sides.

quests.instruction: A square napkin is folded in half, then folded in half again in the other direction. It is unfolded and cut along both fold lines. How many small squares are there?
quests.hint: Picture the two fold lines crossing in the middle of the napkin.
quests.explanation: The two fold lines cross in the middle and split the napkin into four matching pieces. Each piece has four equal sides, so each one is a square.
quests.funFact: Each time you fold paper in half, the number of layers doubles.

quests.instruction: Maya's shape has fewer than four corners and no curved sides. Which shape is it?
quests.hint: Use both clues to rule shapes out. One clue removes shapes with too many corners and the other removes curves.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has four corners, so it is out. A circle has fewer than four corners, but its edge is curved, so it is out too. A triangle has three corners and straight sides.
quests.funFact: Scientists and detectives solve problems by ruling things out one clue at a time.

quests.instruction: Noah draws a triangle. Ruby draws a shape with one more corner than Noah's shape. Which shape could Ruby have drawn?
quests.hint: Count the corners on Noah's shape, then add one.
quests.explanation: A triangle has three corners, so Ruby's shape has four. A rectangle has four corners. A triangle has three and an oval has none.
quests.funFact: Comparing how many more or fewer is a skill used all through math.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is true for both squares and triangles?
quests.hint: Compare what the edges of a square and a triangle are like.
quests.explanation: Squares and triangles are both made of straight sides. A triangle has three corners, not four, and it does not have four sides at all.
quests.funFact: Squares and triangles can be joined together to make bigger shapes.

quests.instruction: A classroom has a round wall clock, a whiteboard, and a door. Which two have the same shape?
quests.hint: Look for the two objects that both have four straight sides.
quests.explanation: The whiteboard and the door are both rectangles, with four straight sides and four square corners. The clock is round, so it is a different shape.
quests.funFact: Most classroom boards are rectangles, which gives lots of room to write in rows.

quests.instruction: How many more corners does a rectangle have than a triangle?
quests.hint: Count the corners on each shape, then find the difference.
quests.explanation: A rectangle has four corners and a triangle has three, so the rectangle has one more.
quests.funFact: Finding the difference between two numbers is called subtraction.

quests.instruction: Using only straight craft sticks joined end to end, which shape can you not build?
quests.hint: Think about what kind of edge a straight stick can make.
quests.explanation: Straight sticks make straight sides, so they can build a triangle or a rectangle. A circle needs a smoothly curved edge, which straight sticks cannot make.
quests.funFact: Many buildings are framed with straight beams, so their outlines are made of straight sides.

quests.instruction: A chocolate bar has 3 rows of 3 equal squares. What shape is the whole bar?
quests.hint: Compare how many pieces go across with how many go down.
quests.explanation: Three squares across and three down means the bar is the same length in both directions, so the whole bar is a square.
quests.funFact: Nine is a square number because 9 small squares can make one bigger square.

quests.instruction: Which list puts the shapes in order from fewest corners to most corners?
quests.hint: Work out the number of corners for each shape first, then line them up.
quests.explanation: A circle has 0 corners, a triangle has 3, and a rectangle has 4, so that order goes from fewest to most.
quests.funFact: Zero is a number too. It tells us there are none.

quests.instruction: Each face of a dice is flat. When you look straight at one face, which flat shape do you see?
quests.hint: Look at one face on its own and count its sides and corners.
quests.explanation: One face of a dice has four equal sides and four square corners, so it is a square.
quests.funFact: On a standard dice, the numbers on opposite faces always add up to seven.

quests.instruction: Hana has a circle, an oval, a triangle, and a square. She puts every shape with no corners in a basket. How many shapes go in the basket?
quests.hint: Decide for each shape whether it has any corners at all.
quests.explanation: The circle and the oval are smooth all the way around, so they go in the basket. The triangle and the square both have corners.
quests.funFact: Sorting by a rule is how scientists, librarians, and shops stay organized.

quests.instruction: Dana reaches into a bag and feels a shape with no corners. It is longer one way than the other. Which shape is it?
quests.hint: Two shapes in the choices have no corners. Think about which one feels the same all the way around.
quests.explanation: A shape with no corners could be a circle or an oval, but a circle is the same distance across everywhere. This one is longer one way, so it is an oval.
quests.funFact: People sometimes use touch alone to tell shapes apart, and your fingers are good at feeling corners.

quests.instruction: A rocket drawing has a rectangle body, one triangle on top, and two small triangles as fins. How many corners do all the triangles have altogether?
quests.hint: Count how many triangles there are first, then think about the corners on each one.
quests.explanation: There are three triangles, and each has three corners, so 3 + 3 + 3 = 9. The corners of the rectangle are not counted.
quests.funFact: Real rockets often have fins near the bottom to help them fly straight.
